Ancestral Heritage Queries

You are the chief archivist of the Sacred Order Bloodline Registry, a hierarchical records system modeled as a rooted tree with N nodes rooted at node 1. Each lineage node's heritage can be efficiently traced through its ancestors.

You receive Q queries. Each query provides a specific node v and an integer k. You must identify the k-th ancestor of node v in the ancestry chain (i.e., the node reached by following exactly k parent links from v). If no such ancestor exists, output -1.
explanation: This is solved using Binary Lifting (Sparse Table for ancestors). During preprocessing, fill up[v][0] = parent of v. Then up[v][j] = up[up[v][j-1]][j-1], i.e., the 2^j-th ancestor of v. For each query (v, k), decompose k in binary and jump through the precomputed ancestors accordingly. Preprocessing: O(N log N). Query: O(log N). Total: O((N + Q) log N).
